title: Anchored Divergence: Immanent Critique as Survival Strategy Under Tail-Loss, and the Mandala as Limit Case (EA-SEI-ANCHDIV-01 v1.0)
creator: Lee Sharks
description:
The second paper in a four-part June 2026 cycle, by Lee Sharks. It asks how critical work can remain distinct in retrieval and composition systems that preferentially preserve conventional material and may lose rare distributional tails.

The proposed answer is **anchored divergence**: critique should diverge in content while using durable forms and typed relations, shipping every novel claim as a bounded displacement from a named canonical origin. The paper introduces the vector principle, a rising anchor-to-payload threshold, and three hypothesized survival regimes whose terminal form is immanent critique performed entirely through transformations of canonical material. The archive’s Mandala operator system is presented as a limit case. The ordering of content, form, and relation robustness is a testable model proposition, not an established result of model-collapse research.
